title: 6. 12-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet Audit
book_title: Chapter 6: The Forensic Ledger — Margins, Cash Conversion & Capital Dilution

epigraph.quote: Profit is an opinion formed by depreciation schedules; cash flow from operations is a fact settled at the bank.
epigraph.author: Forensic Accounting Maxim

web_blocks.html: A 12-year forensic sweep of Tanfac's audited financials (FY2015–FY2026, plus the September 2026 balance sheet) shows two clear shifts [1]. First, the company moved from a leveraged turnaround into a debt-free cash generator between FY2015 and FY2024 [1]. Second, it transitioned into an equity-fortified, capex-heavy growth platform during FY2025–Sep 2026 [1]. Over the decade, median sales growth stands at 22.4% [1]. Revenue compounded from ₹120 crore in FY2015 to ₹711 crore in FY2026, reaching ₹784 crore TTM through September 2026 [1].

web_blocks.caption: Tanfac Industries — 12-Year Profit & Loss Statement (FY2015–FY2026 & TTM, ₹ Cr) [1]
web_blocks.takeaway: Revenue scaled nearly 6x from ₹120 Cr (FY15) to ₹711 Cr (FY26), but OPM compressed from 24% in FY25 to 16% in FY26 and 14% TTM as peak scarcity spreads normalized and depreciation rose to ₹17 Cr.

web_blocks.html: Margin Bridge & Profitability Forensics: Operating profit peaked at ₹131 crore (24% OPM) in FY2025 on ₹557 crore of sales [1]. In FY2026, revenue grew ₹154 crore (+28% YoY to ₹711 crore), yet operating profit slipped to ₹114 crore (16% OPM) [1]. Meanwhile, depreciation jumped 70% from ₹10 crore to ₹17 crore as new AHF and Solar DHF assets entered service [1]. Net profit fell 20% from ₹88 crore in FY2025 to ₹70 crore in FY2026 (EPS ₹35.16 vs ₹44.08) [1]. The September 2026 quarter saw OPM ease further to 12%, with ₹27 crore operating profit on ₹230 crore sales [1]. Return ratios followed suit: ROCE moderated from 42% in FY2025 to 23.9% in FY2026, while ROE held at 20.3% (3-year average ROE 25.1%) [1].

web_blocks.caption: Tanfac Industries — Balance Sheet Evolution (FY2015–FY2026 & Sep 2026, ₹ Cr) [1]
web_blocks.takeaway: Mid-2026 QIP (₹250 Cr) and preferential equity doubled Reserves from ₹363 Cr (Mar 2026) to ₹726 Cr (Sep 2026) while CWIP surged to ₹153 Cr for the ₹495 Cr R-32 expansion.

web_blocks.html: Balance Sheet, Debt & Dilution Forensics: Between FY2020 and FY2024, Tanfac carried zero borrowings [1]. To bridge capex before mid-2026 equity raises, debt rose to ₹41 crore in FY2025 and ₹93 crore in FY2026 [1]. By September 2026, borrowings reached ₹136 crore—still modest against ₹737 crore of net worth [1]. That net worth includes ₹11 crore Equity Capital and ₹726 crore Reserves, lifted by a ₹250 crore QIP and ~₹99.41 crore preferential issue [1][4]. Equity Capital edged up from ₹10 crore to ₹11 crore in September 2026, marking ~10% dilution [1]. ICRA reaffirmed [ICRA]A+ Stable / [ICRA]A1+ in October 2026 on this conservative leverage [4]. Fixed Assets grew 3.9x from ₹61 crore in FY2024 to ₹237 crore in September 2026, with ₹153 crore more in Capital Work-in-Progress (CWIP) [1].

web_blocks.caption: Tanfac Industries — Cash Flow & Free Cash Flow Forensics (FY2015–FY2026, ₹ Cr) [1]
web_blocks.takeaway: CFO/EBITDA conversion dropped from 73–121% (FY15–FY24) to 47% in FY25 and 56% in FY26, while heavy capex pushed Free Cash Flow negative (-₹64 Cr in FY25, -₹39 Cr in FY26).

web_blocks.caption: Tanfac Industries — Working Capital & Efficiency Ratios (FY2015–FY2026) [1]
web_blocks.takeaway: Days Payable compressed from 77 days (FY24) to 21 days (FY26), driving the Cash Conversion Cycle up to 115 days despite lower inventory days (79 days).

web_blocks.html: Working Capital & Cash Conversion Forensics: Cash conversion is the sharpest yellow flag in the forensic ledger. From FY2015 through FY2024, Tanfac converted 73% to 121% of EBITDA into pre-tax operating cash flow [1]. In FY2025 and FY2026, CFO/EBITDA dropped to 47% and 56% respectively [1]. Operating cash flow stagnated at ₹33 crore (FY25) and ₹43 crore (FY26) even as EBITDA hit ₹114–₹131 crore [1]. Why did cash lag profit? Debtor Days climbed from 28 days in FY2022 to 57–65 days in FY2025–FY2026 [1]. Meanwhile, Days Payable shrank from 77 days in FY2024 to 21 days in FY2026, stretching the Cash Conversion Cycle to 115 days [1]. Combined with ₹82–₹97 crore annual capex, Free Cash Flow turned negative (-₹64 crore in FY25, -₹39 crore in FY26) [1].

Asset-Turn & Depreciation Forensics: Comparing Fixed Assets plus CWIP against sales highlights the lag between spending and revenue [1]. In FY2024, Tanfac generated ₹378 crore of sales on just ₹61 crore of net Fixed Assets [1]. That was an exceptional 6.2x fixed-asset turnover on older, depreciated kilns [1]. By September 2026, net Fixed Assets reached ₹237 crore alongside ₹153 crore of CWIP [1]. Total productive capital hit ₹390 crore against ₹784 crore of TTM revenue [1]. Blended fixed-asset turnover has stepped down toward ~3.3x on commissioned blocks [1]. Depreciation also climbed from ₹7 crore (FY24) to ₹10 crore (FY25), ₹17 crore (FY26), and ₹19 crore TTM [1]. Once the ₹153 crore CWIP and remaining R-32 outlay capitalize in FY2027, annual depreciation will rise further [1][4]. That raises the hurdle for operating profit growth just to hold net margins steady [1][4].

Quarterly Inflection Check (Q2 FY2027 / Sep 2026): Quarterly data through September 2026 confirms both top-line momentum and near-term margin pressure [1]. Quarterly sales hit ₹230 crore (+37% YoY vs ₹169 crore in Sep 2025), yet operating profit stayed flat at ₹27 crore [1]. That pushed OPM down to 12% versus 16% a year earlier [1]. Interest edged up to ₹2 crore and depreciation reached ₹5 crore [1]. Net profit stood at ₹19 crore, aided by ₹4 crore of other income—likely treasury yield on unspent QIP cash [1]. Near-term earnings clearly lean on treasury income while core spreads await the Solar DHF and Japanese ramp-up [1][4].

book_paragraphs: Now let us open the twelve-year forensic ledger—from March 2015 through March 2026, plus the September 2026 balance sheet. Let the audited numbers speak without spin. Over this twelve-year span, Tanfac grew sales from ₹120 crore to ₹711 crore, a median annual pace of 22.4%. That top-line arc is impressive, yet a forensic auditor never stops at the top line.

Look first at the margin bridge. In FY2025, Tanfac earned ₹131 crore of operating profit on ₹557 crore of revenue—a 24% operating margin—and ₹88 crore of net profit. In FY2026, revenue jumped ₹154 crore to ₹711 crore, yet operating profit fell to ₹114 crore (16% OPM). Depreciation jumped 70% from ₹10 crore to ₹17 crore, interest tripled from ₹2 crore (in FY24) to ₹6 crore, and net profit dropped 20% to ₹70 crore. By the September 2026 quarter, quarterly OPM eased further to 12%. That is the textbook signature of capacity-led volume growth colliding with margin normalization and higher depreciation.

Next, examine the balance sheet and share dilution. For five straight years from FY2020 through FY2024, Tanfac carried zero debt. In FY2025 and FY2026, borrowings returned—₹41 crore, then ₹93 crore, then ₹136 crore by September 2026. Fixed assets more than tripled from ₹61 crore in FY2024 to ₹237 crore in September 2026, with ₹153 crore more in Capital Work-in-Progress. To prevent debt from spiraling, Tanfac raised ₹250 crore via QIP and ₹99.41 crore via preferential allotment in mid-2026. That lifted reserves from ₹363 crore to ₹726 crore and nudged equity capital from ₹10 crore to ₹11 crore. That ~10% dilution kept leverage conservative enough for ICRA to reaffirm its [ICRA]A+ Stable rating in October 2026.

Finally, look at the cash-flow statement, where the sharpest yellow flag waves. Between FY2015 and FY2024, Tanfac converted 73% to 121% of operating profit into cash. In FY2025 and FY2026, CFO-to-EBITDA dropped to 47% and 56%, leaving CFO at just ₹43 crore in FY2026 against ₹70 crore of net profit. The culprit sits in working capital. Debtor Days widened from 28 days in FY2022 to 57 days in FY2026, while Days Payable fell from 77 days in FY2024 to just 21 days in FY2026. That stretched the Cash Conversion Cycle to 115 days. Add ₹82 crore of capex, and Free Cash Flow printed negative ₹64 crore in FY2025 and negative ₹39 crore in FY2026. Until the new R-32 and Solar DHF plants generate cash faster than working capital absorbs it, free cash flow stays on a leash.

Put all four financial statements together and a clear picture emerges. Tanfac is no longer the fragile, debt-laden commodity maker of FY2015. Nor is it yet a self-funding, high-conversion specialty compounder. It is a well-capitalized mid-cap builder sitting on ₹737 crore of net worth and ₹390 crore of fixed assets and CWIP. Its ultimate return on capital will be decided over FY2027 and FY2028.

One more ratio deserves attention before we close the ledger: fixed-asset turnover and the coming depreciation wave. Back in FY2024, Tanfac squeezed ₹378 crore of sales out of ₹61 crore of net fixed assets—an extraordinary 6.2 times asset turn on old kilns. By September 2026, net fixed assets climbed nearly fourfold to ₹237 crore, with ₹153 crore in Capital Work-in-Progress waiting to be capitalized. As those new stainless-steel reactors hit the depreciation schedule, annual depreciation has climbed from ₹7 crore in FY2024 to ₹19 crore trailing twelve-month, and it will rise further in FY2027.

Look at the September 2026 quarter as a live preview of that transition. Revenue surged 37% year-over-year to a record ₹230 crore, yet operating profit stayed flat at ₹27 crore as margins eased to 12%. Net profit held steady at ₹19 crore partly thanks to ₹4 crore of other income—almost certainly treasury interest on unspent QIP cash. That tells you where Tanfac stands today: the balance sheet is flush, the top line is expanding, and now the operating plants must earn their keep.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: When CFO-to-EBITDA drops from 80%+ to 47–56% for two straight years while Debtor Days double and Payable Days shrink to 21, the business is funding growth out of working capital. The mid-2026 QIP replenished the treasury, but durable compounding requires CFO to catch up with PAT.

book_subsections.title: ROCE Normalization and the Capital-Base Denominator
paragraphs: Tanfac's ROCE fell from 42% in FY2025 to 23.9% in FY2026, with ROE at 20.3%. That drop is mechanical as well as cyclical. Not only did EBIT soften, but the capital base expanded rapidly via ₹237 crore of fixed assets, ₹153 crore of CWIP, and ₹349 crore of fresh equity. Once those assets commission in FY2027, ROCE will recover only if the Japanese contract and Solar DHF lines deliver strong asset turns.

book_subsections.title: Dividend Payout Conservatism During Expansion
paragraphs: Dividend payout dropped from 17% in FY2022 to 10% in FY2025 and 7% in FY2026. Retaining 93% of earnings while raising external equity makes sense during a ₹495 crore capex cycle, provided the incremental capital earns above its cost.

book_subsections.title: Treasury Cushion vs. Core Operating Earnings
paragraphs: Whenever a company raises ₹349 crore of fresh equity mid-year, short-term treasury income temporarily flatters Profit Before Tax. Separating core operating EBIT from non-operating interest income ensures we never mistake unspent QIP cash yields for chemical-plant profitability.

book_subsections.title: Twelve-Year Capital Allocation: From Survival to Scale
paragraphs: Step back and look at how Tanfac allocated every rupee of cash across twelve years. From FY2015 through FY2019, Cash from Operating Activities totaled ₹115 crore. Almost all of it went toward paying down ₹57 crore of debt and stabilizing the legacy Cuddalore plant. From FY2020 through FY2024, CFO totaled ₹180 crore while borrowings stayed at zero. That allowed Tanfac to fund early brownfield expansions and build a ₹67 crore investment cushion without diluting shareholders.

In FY2025 and FY2026, the capital-allocation regime inverted completely. CFO was ₹33 crore and ₹43 crore respectively, while Cash from Investing Activities absorbed ₹42 crore in FY2025 and ₹91 crore in FY2026. Free Cash Flow turned negative by ₹103 crore cumulatively over two years. Because internal cash could not fund a ₹495 crore R-32 build-out on top of working-capital absorption, Tanfac tapped both debt (₹136 crore by September 2026) and equity (₹349 crore via QIP and preferential allotment). Over FY2027 and FY2028, the forensic verdict hinges on one simple test: do those ₹390 crore of fixed assets and CWIP start throwing off ₹100 crore-plus of annual operating cash flow?
